title: der, die, das: every noun has a gender (Die Artikel)
summary: Every German noun is der, die or das. Learn how to live with it: always learn the article with the noun, and use a few reliable patterns.
goals: Name everyday objects with the right article
Use the patterns that almost always work (-ung, -e, -chen, -in)

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 5: Things (Was ist das?, Wem gehört das?)

sections.title: Three genders
sections.text:
Every German noun has a gender: masculine (**der**), feminine (**die**) or neuter (**das**). It is grammar, not meaning: [[der Tisch]], [[die Lampe]], [[das Fenster]].

'A / an' follows the gender too: [[ein Tisch]], [[eine Lampe]], [[ein Fenster]].

The one rule that matters most: **always learn a noun together with its article.** Not 'Tisch = table' but 'der Tisch'. Your word cards already do this.

sections.title: Why this is hard for you, and what helps
sections.text:
Russian has genders too, and sometimes they match: [[der Tisch]] and стол are masculine, [[die Tür]] and дверь feminine, [[das Fenster]] and окно neuter. But often they don't: книга is feminine, [[das Buch]] is neuter. So never copy the Russian gender.

Russian has no articles. Armenian has articles (գիրքը = the book, մի գիրք = a book) but no gender. So 'the' vs 'a' is familiar to you; what is new is that the article also shows the gender. That makes der/die/das the hardest part of German for you. Every learner struggles here; what helps is repetition, not more rules.

sections.title: Patterns that (almost) always work
rows: -e (most nouns; but der for male people and a few others: der Kollege, der Name)
-chen (small versions of things; always das, even for people: das Mädchen, the girl)
-er (people who do something; but die Mutter, die Schwester, die Tochter)

sections.title: How to remember
sections.text: Say nouns with their article every time, even in your head: [[der Stift]], [[die Tasche]], [[das Handy]]. Some learners picture der words as blue, die words as red and das words as green. And if you guess wrong in a conversation, people still understand you.

sections.title: Listen and repeat: noun plus article

items.question: Which article goes with Tisch?
items.explanation: der Tisch. Learn it as one unit: der Tisch.

items.question: Which of these nouns is feminine (die)?
items.explanation: die Tasche. Most nouns ending in -e are feminine.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: That's a mobile phone.
items.explanation: das Handy is neuter, so ein Handy.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: The lamp is new.
items.explanation: die Lampe. At the start of the sentence: Die.
